title: Danh Vo
subtitle: Danh Vo Güldenhof
body:
Inspired by the continual transformation he observes while gardening on his farm north of Berlin, Danh Vo brings together living matter with old and new works for his first Canadian museum exhibition. Flowers entangled in fish bones and mushrooms sprouting from bronze bodies merge the organic and inorganic in a singular sculptural vocabulary. His materials include calligraphy and drawings made by his father alongside sculpture and ceramic fragments from diverse historical worlds. Here, centuries-old forms — objects marked by devotion, trade, migration, conflict and intimacy — enter into circulation with newly made bronze sculptures, all brought together by Vo in unexpected ways.

Danh Vo is organized by The Shen Foundation in collaboration with The Art Gallery of Ontario. The exhibition is curated by Adam Welch, Carol and Morton Rapp Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art, in collaboration with Kitty Scott, Director and Curator, at The Shen Foundation.
